judge.voice: The check itself was fine. I answered five logistics tasks on my phone, and nobody asked me anything strange about Ukraine. My "як це" was accepted, which I liked. But it put me at C1 "Fluent". I know that's not true. I make mistakes with articles, and "explain me" is wrong, yet it told me "no real mistakes". That makes me doubt every correction it gives. The advice, "say a little more in each answer", is useless to me. I already write long answers, and I told it my interview is on Friday. Sure, it mentioned interview answers in one sentence, but nothing was specific to it. One task was cut off mid-sentence. I would try the interview scenario, because the tasks felt like my job. But I wouldn't trust the level, and I wouldn't recommend it until the placement is honest.

Mark Ellis · hiring manager
Thanks for coming in today. Could you tell me about your current logistics job? What does a normal day look like for you?
You · written

Then I communicate with carriers and drivers, and I make plan for the loading. Also I am responsible about the dispečink and about the documents for delivery.
Mark Ellis · hiring manager
Thank you, that gives me a clear picture of your day. You mention carriers and drivers a lot. What do you do when a delivery is late?
You · written
When delivery is late, first I call the driver and I ask where he is and what is the reason. Then I inform the customer about the new time of arrival. If it is big problem, I find another carrier or I change the plan for the loading. After that I write the report for my manager.
Mark Ellis · hiring manager
Calling the driver first gives you the facts quickly, which is smart. When the problem is big, what makes you choose another carrier instead of waiting?
You · written
I choose another carrier when the delay is more than two hours or when the driver cannot tell me the exact time. Also if the cargo is urgent, for example fresh food, I cannot wait. Mark Ellis · hiring manager
That's impressive, the customer still got the goods the same day. What do you usually do first when a driver goes quiet for a while?
You · written
First I check the last GPS position of the truck and I write to the driver in the messenger. If he does not answer in thirty minutes, I call him and also I call the dispečink of the carrier. I want to know is the driver ok and where is the cargo.

judge.voice: The questions felt like a real logistics interview, and Mark Ellis followed what I said, which I liked. Both corrections were right, and "for three years" is exactly my usual mistake. Nobody treated me like a Czech learner, and my "dispečink" wasn't a problem. But it says my level is C1 · Fluent. I'm not, and that makes me doubt the rest. It also let "responsible about" and "it is big problem" pass without a word. I wanted more interview phrases, and I only got "chase up" at the end. After four replies it said mission done, which was short. I'd use it again for a few nights before Friday, but I'd want the level fixed and more vocabulary for my role.
